Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

gsm.safety v1.2.0 (Upcoming)

See it move: the annotated v1.2.0 demo has captures, try-it steps and the detail behind everything below.

gsm.safety v1.2.0 brings the widgets up to safety.viz v1.12.0 and rebuilds the safety census on qualified metrics. Two published clinical figures change: the eDISH chart no longer reads a baseline as a peak, and the bundled study’s death count goes from 2 to 12. SafetyCensus() keeps its name and its arguments. Its figures are qualified on gsm.core 1.3.2.

What’s new

  • The death count reads both death sources and counts only enrolled participants. It joins the death domain to a discontinuation reason of death, in any case. On the bundled study it reports 12 of 754 where SafetyCensus() reported 2. obot.roadmap#274, #56, PR #57, #168, PR #169
  • The safety census is twelve metrics, each published beside its own denominator. Four more figures move on the bundled study: randomised 567 (was blank), received study drug 679 (was 599), disposition 94 (was 116), and the ECG figure reads absent, not blank. obot.roadmap#274, #61, PR #62, #66, PR #67
  • The eDISH chart no longer counts a participant’s baseline as an on-treatment peak. The bundle moves from safety.viz v1.4.0 to v1.12.0. On the example data 23 participants’ peaks fall; Hy’s Law drops from 28 to 13. obot.roadmap#164, safety.viz#91, #49, PR #51, #165, PR #169
  • Every chart safety.viz draws can be drawn from R. Four widgets are new, making thirteen: Widget_HepWaterfall(), Widget_NepExplorer(), Widget_TimeToEvent() and Widget_ParticipantProfile(). obot.roadmap#164, obot.roadmap#165, #49, PR #51, #71, PR #72
  • Four widgets take the Visit | Study day toggle. The participant profile, hep-explorer, outlier explorer and QT explorer accept x_axis in lSettings; the hep waterfall reads DY as its study day. The example data now carries DY and ABLFL. obot.roadmap#438, #166, PR #167
  • The FDA safety guide’s appendix tables, and three of its rules, are in R. FDA_AbnormalityLevels and FDA_ExtremeValues are package data, and Derive_ULNMultiple(), Derive_AbnormalityLevel() and Derive_ExtremeValueFlag() apply them. obot.roadmap#9, #77, PR #83, #78, PR #86, #79, PR #84, #80, PR #85

Deprecated

  • SafetyCensus()’s column arguments are deprecated and ignored; no release removing them is set yet. strArmCol, strReasonCol, chrDeathValues and the rest still run, warn, and change no figure, because each metric declares the columns it reads. Pass the mapped domains instead, including the new dfDeath and dfRandomization. #66, PR #67

Removed

  • The histogram’s test_normality and compare_distributions settings. safety.viz no longer draws p-values on the histogram, so drop them from your calls. #158, PR #163

Also in this release

  • The QT explorer averages replicate readings, so its n counts participants. #158, PR #163
  • BuildWidgetPayload() refuses a setting it cannot send, naming it: a missing limit-of-normal column, a value that is not one string, NULL, a group that is not a list, or too few rows. #99, PR #101, #103, PR #104, #109, PR #113, #125, PR #130, #149, PR #150
  • The participant profile refuses malformed adverse-event settings, and the examples drop placeholder adverse-event rows. #107, PR #112, #119, PR #122, PR #124, #139, PR #140
  • SafetyCensus() names bad input instead of counting it: an infinite day count, a domain without the ID column, a group column the subjects lack or that collides with the ID, and settings given as a data.frame. #96, PR #97, #117, PR #118, #126, PR #131, #144, PR #146, #133, PR #134
  • The report writers refuse an output file or directory that is missing, empty or not one string. #106, PR #111, #115, PR #116, #143, PR #145, #120, PR #123, #135, PR #136
  • The derivations refuse to overwrite an input column, and a frame already carrying AbnormalityDirection is refused too. The requirement matrix now describes grading as shipped. #102, PR #105, #128, PR #132
  • The qualification records ship inside the package, and the suite checks every figure in them against the code. #63, PR #64, #153, PR #154
  • Dependencies install from Gilead-Public, and four workflows that failed before starting run again. #160, PR #161, #55, PR #73
  • The package site wears the hub’s theme, and the repository carries the CLAUDE.md its guidelines ask for. PR #94, PR #95, #81, PR #82
  • Four things are knowingly not in this release: data completeness in the census, an ECG figure (gsm.mapping maps no ECG domain), the Patient Journey Explorer widget, and a ruling on three charts’ JavaScript confidence intervals. #58, #172, obot.roadmap#350, safety.viz#259

Tests and provenance

4,640 tests pass against gsm.core 1.3.2, gsm.mapping 1.2.0 and gsm.reporting 1.1.8. Every census figure is measured twice, by two routes that share no code. The vendored bundle is byte-identical to safety.viz v1.12.0 (122ec3f), which the parity check confirms.

gsm.safety v1.1.0

See it move: the annotated v1.1 demo walks the new metrics running live on the DEMO-301 study site, with captures and try-it-yourself steps.

gsm.safety could draw the eDISH chart but could not tell you how many participants were in the Hy’s Law quadrant. This release adds the metrics phase that answers that — three participant-level safety metrics plus the denominators a safety overview leads with — and moves the report workflows into the standard gsm phase layout on the way. One path changes: workflows formerly under inst/workflow/3_reports/ now live in inst/workflow/4_modules/.

What’s new

  • A 2_metrics workflow phase: three participant-level safety metrics (#45, PR #47; hub obot.roadmap#138). saf0001 Hy’s Law candidate, saf0002 QTcF prolongation, and saf0003 serious / related AE — each scores one row per participant with an ordinal tier through the standard gsm contract (Analyze_Identity() + Flag(), following gsm.kri’s pat0015 precedent), so subject-level rows land in Reporting_Results beside site and country rows with nothing downstream changing. The liver and QT cut-points come from the vendored data contracts of the charts they correspond to, so the metric and the chart cannot drift apart. Measured on demo data before being treated as real (the hub#138 gate): 9 / 11 / 68 red-tier participants of 765 scored. See them live.
  • SafetyCensus() (PR #47) — reduces the mapped domains to the denominators a safety overview leads with: enrollment, exposure, person-years, deaths, and data coverage per visit — the figure that decides whether a quiet visit is reassuring or empty. New exported helpers behind the metrics: Input_HysLaw(), Input_QtProlongation(), Input_SafetyAE().
  • Report workflows move to inst/workflow/4_modules/ (#46, PR #47; hub obot.roadmap#136) — the standard gsm phase directory for meta.Type: Report workflows, the one gsm.kri already uses. Update any pipeline that globbed 3_reports/.

1 286 tests pass; R CMD check clean.
